_meta.indication: Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (3:2 ANDEMBRY:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of 6 months duration.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with Type I or Type II HAE who experienced at least 2 investigator-confirmed HAE attacks over a 2-month period prior to treatment.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Monthly HAE attack rate at 6 months (number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per month).
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean monthly HAE attack rate 0.22 (ANDEMBRY) vs 2.07 (placebo); 89.2% reduction relative to placebo; p < 0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥7%) are nasopharyngitis (21% vs 12% placebo) and abdominal pain (8% vs 0% placebo).
target_moa: Inhibitor of activated Factor XII (FXIIa) that binds its catalytic domain, decreasing prekallikrein-to-kallikrein activation and bradykinin generation involved in HAE attacks.
modality: Monoclonal antibody (recombinant, fully human IgG4/A-light chain).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was held; the application did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues.

basis.text: Garadacimab received Fast Track Designation on December 14, 2021.

citations.quote: Garadacimab received Fast Track Designation on December 14, 2021, and orphan drug designation on April 30, 2020.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation granted April 30, 2020 for bradykinin-mediated angioedema (which includes hereditary angioedema).

citations.quote: Garadacimab was granted Orphan Drug Designation in April 2020 for bradykinin-mediated angioedema (which includes hereditary angioedema) and is therefore exempt from Pediatric Research Equity Act study requirements.

summary.text: Standard-review BLA supported by a single phase 3 trial; garadacimab held Fast Track Designation and Orphan Drug Designation, with no advisory committee held.
